consensus_findings: Across the canonized KO runs, FY2025 keeps most of the prior Item 1A architecture and should be read as selective sharpening rather than a dramatic rewrite.
The useful signal clusters around health-policy and demand pressure, product-quality and recall execution, bottler concentration, partner-conduct spillover, and updated Pillar Two detail.
The two primary-read runs broadly agree that the first read remains useful on a mostly stable filing without forcing significance into routine upkeep.
The two Fresh vs reused runs broadly agree that freshness stays narrow on KO and that most movement belongs in broadened carryover or boundary buckets.
disagreement_findings: The primary read remains the best first read because it keeps the broader filing shift legible while staying restrained.
Fresh vs reused adds value by sorting genuinely fresh specifics from reused structure, but it is narrower and more classification-sensitive than the primary read.
The extra 2025 specifics beyond Pillar Two are not identical across the two Fresh vs reused runs, which is why KO works as a restraint test rather than a novelty showcase.
why_this_case_matters: KO matters because it is the lower-drift restraint case: the filing is mostly stable, but the useful signal is still visible when the product stays disciplined about selective sharpening rather than hunting for drama.
investor_read: The investor read is not that Coca-Cola suddenly rewrote its risk map. It is that FY2025 makes a few areas more decision-useful by sharpening health-policy pressure on sweetened beverages, broadening product-quality and recall execution risk, naming bottler concentration more explicitly, and updating Pillar Two developments with dated 2025 to 2026 specifics.
protocol_read: Methodologically, KO is useful because it shows whether the product can remain helpful when the filing pair is stable. The answer is yes, but only when the primary read stays restrained and Fresh vs reused remains narrow about what is actually new versus what is better read as broadened carryover or reused structure.
caveat: This remains a bounded case view. KO improves credibility because it is a lower-drift restraint case, but it does not justify broad issuer expansion, whole-filing overlays, or equal-weight promotion of Fresh vs reused.
